blocks.title: Which work orders count
items: Finished work orders: “Completed”, “Invoiced”, “Paid”, “Archived”.
A work order's day is its completion date in Kyiv time; the period includes both days.

items.text: excl. VAT — the base of profit and margin
amount incl. VAT minus amount excl. VAT; work orders completed before 08.10.2026 in “VAT on top” mode give VAT 0
what was billed to customers

blocks.title: Labor and parts
items: From the actual work order lines and also excl. VAT: “Labor” + “Parts” = “Amount” (up to rounding).

workOrders.title: How the “Work orders” report is calculated

items: Standard hours and labor amounts of work orders — by mechanic.

blocks.title: Which work orders count
items: By the work order document date — as in the work order list filter, not by creation date.
Cancelled ones are not counted; drafts are, as in the list.

blocks.title: Opening a row
items: A mechanic's row opens their work orders with the same period and statuses (all except cancelled) — the list matches the report.

items.text: remaining quantity of each batch of the product in this warehouse × batch price; quantity outside batches — at the product purchase price
quantity × current product sale price

blocks.title: Also
items: Stock is as of now: the period dates do not affect it.
Available = quantity − reserved.
A product deleted from the catalogue but still in stock stays in the report and totals, marked “deleted”.

items.text: the counterparty owes us
we owe the counterparty

blocks.title: Where the balance comes from
items: The balance is the sum of the counterparty's entries: the entry type alone sets its sign (charge, payment, refund…), the amount is always positive.
The balance is kept in the base currency: an entry in another currency is converted at the rate.

items.text: total duration of the lift's calendar records starting in the period
working days of the lift's branch in the period × length of its working day (“Settings” → “Working days”)
busy / working time, with one decimal place

blocks.title: Special cases
items: A branch without settings — 09:00–18:00, Mon–Fri.
A day off adds no working time; a period of days off only — 0 %.
Lifts with no records in the period — in one “N more…” row.

blocks.title: Which work orders count
items: Finished work orders (“Completed”, “Invoiced”, “Paid”, “Archived”) by completion date; revenue excl. VAT.

items.text: quantity × cost of the batch it was taken from; without it — the product purchase price
labor excl. VAT × labor share ({{pct}}) — an estimate of mechanics' pay; the owner and admins change it in “Report settings”

blocks.title: Profit and margin
items: Gross profit = revenue excl. VAT − cost; margin is its share of revenue.
“Normal” — margin of {{norm}} % or more.
The labor share does not go into P&L: it uses accrued payroll.
Accrual method; everything excl. VAT, in the base currency; a month is a Kyiv calendar month.

items.text: finished work orders by completion date — as in “Profitability”
quantity × batch cost; without it — the product purchase price
accrued in computed and paid payroll periods; a period spanning months is split between them by days
by category: cash — “Expense” always, other outflows per the settings; bank — lines allocated as “Expense”
cash receipts with an income category — per the settings (manual deposit by default)
exchange gain minus exchange loss

blocks.title: Net profit
items: Gross profit − payroll − operating expenses + other income + exchange differences.
Salary payouts, supplier payments and customer refunds are not expenses — they are already in payroll, cost and revenue.

items.text: VAT of “Sent”, “Partially paid”, “Paid”, “Overdue” invoices by document date; drafts and cancelled are excluded
VAT of received purchases — “Partial” and “Received” supplier orders by document date; drafts and not yet received are excluded

items: A difference above 0 is payable, below 0 — refundable.
